facts.statement: The genus Turfanosuchus was described by C.C. Young in 1973.
facts.quote: authority: Young, 1973

facts.statement: The type species T. dabanensis was based on a partially complete, disarticulated skeleton found in the Kelamayi Formation of the Turfan Basin.
facts.quote: based on a partially complete but disarticulated fossil skeleton (IVPP V.32237) found in the Kelamayi Formation of the Turfan Basin

facts.statement: Turfanosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic (Anisian) in northwestern China.
facts.quote: lived during the Middle Triassic (Anisian) of northwestern China

facts.statement: Turfanosuchus is likely a member of the family Gracilisuchidae within the archosaurs.
facts.quote: likely a gracilisuchid archosaur

facts.statement: A 2014 study grouped Turfanosuchus with Gracilisuchus and Yonghesuchus in the family Gracilisuchidae.
facts.quote: a 2014 study grouped these three genera in the family Gracilisuchidae

facts.statement: Turfanosuchus possessed teeth on its palate and internal carotid arteries entering the braincase from below.
facts.quote: It possessed teeth on the palate, and internal carotid arteries which entered the braincase from below

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Turfanosuchus projects a small prong behind the nostrils.
facts.quote: The premaxilla (a toothed bone at the tip of the snout) projects a small prong behind the nares (nostril holes)

facts.statement: The maxilla of Turfanosuchus features a rare posterodorsal process.
facts.quote: The maxilla (the main toothed bone of the snout) also had a posterodorsal process

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Turfanosuchus likely had five teeth in the premaxilla and at least 13 in the maxilla.
facts.quote: The premaxilla probably had five teeth, while the maxilla had at least 13

facts.statement: The preserved teeth of Turfanosuchus were curved and finely serrated.
facts.quote: Preserved teeth were curved and finely serrated

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Turfanosuchus contained at least 16 teeth.
facts.quote: There were at least 16 teeth in the lower jaw

facts.statement: Among gracilisuchids, Turfanosuchus is unique in having a lower jaw prong much longer than the upper prong.
facts.quote: Unique to Turfanosuchus among gracilisuchids, the lower prong was much longer than the upper prong

facts.statement: The outer surface of the surangular bone in Turfanosuchus is highly concave, a unique trait.
facts.quote: Another autapomorphy of Turfanosuchus is how the outer surface of the surangular was highly concave

facts.statement: Although initially thought to lack them, one osteoderm was later found on the skeleton of Turfanosuchus.
facts.quote: Osteoderms (bony plates) were initially reported as being absent, but later preparation revealed one

facts.statement: The heel bone of Turfanosuchus shares many similarities with those of crurotarsan archosauriforms.
facts.quote: The calcaneum (heel bone) had many similarities with that of "crurotarsan" archosauriforms

facts.statement: Wu & Russell (2001) classified Turfanosuchus as a non-archosaur archosauriform based on its pterygoid teeth.
facts.quote: Wu & Russell (2001) used this to justify classifying Turfanosuchus as a non-archosaur archosauriform

facts.statement: Recent findings of pterygoid teeth in other crown-archosaurs suggest Turfanosuchus may be a crown-archosaur.
facts.quote: However, more recently pterygoid teeth have been reported in crown-archosaurs such as Eoraptor, Eudimorphodon, Lewisuchus, Eodromaeus, and Yonghesuchus

facts.statement: Like other diapsids, Turfanosuchus had two openings at the rear of its skull known as temporal fenestrae.
facts.quote: As with other diapsids, Turfanosuchus had a pair of openings at the rear portion of the skull known as temporal fenestra

facts.statement: Turfanosuchus is an extinct genus of archosauriform reptile meaning "Turfan basin crocodile".
facts.quote: Turfanosuchus (que significa "cocodrilo de la cuenca de Turfan") es un género extinto de reptil arcosauriforme

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Middle Triassic, specifically the Anisian stage, approximately 240 to 237 million years ago in what is now China.
facts.quote: vivió durante el Triásico Medio, específicamente en el período Anisiense, hace unos 240 a 237 millones de años en lo que hoy es China

facts.statement: The type species T. dabanensis was described by C.C. Young in 1973 based on a partially complete and disarticulated fossil skeleton (IVPP V.32237).
facts.quote: La especie tipo, T. dabanensis, fue descrita por C.C. Young en 1973, basándose en un esqueleto fósil parcialmente completo y desarticulado (IVPP V.32237)

facts.statement: Young originally believed the fossils came from an animal similar to Euparkeria and assigned it to the family Euparkeriidae.
facts.quote: Young originalmente creyó que los fósiles provenían de un animal similar a Euparkeria, y lo asignó a la familia Euparkeriidae

facts.statement: The fossil was not fully prepared at the time of the initial description.
facts.quote: El fósil, sin embargo, no estaba completamente preparado

facts.statement: Subsequent analysis by Parrish in 1993 indicated that the fossils represented a suchian.
facts.quote: Análisis posteriores hechos por Parrish en 1993 indicaron que los fósiles representaban a un suquio

facts.statement: In 2001, Xiao-Chun Wu and Anthony Russell redescribed the fossil.
facts.quote: En 2001, Xiao-Chun Wu (del Instituto de Paleontología de Vertebrados y Paleoantropología en Pekín) y Anthony Russell (de la Universidad de Calgary) redescribieron el fósil

facts.statement: Wu and Russell noted that the limb bones (femur and humerus) resembled those of Ticinosuchus and Euparkeria, though the calcaneum did not.
facts.quote: Wu y Russell prepararon el fósil, y notaron que los huesos de las extremidades (fémur y húmero) se parecían a los de Ticinosuchus y Euparkeria, aunque el calcáneo no

facts.statement: Further preparation revealed a partial osteoderm.
facts.quote: Preparación adicional reveló un osteodermo parcial

facts.statement: Wu and Russell concluded that Turfanosuchus was not a suchian nor even a member of the Crurotarsi.
facts.quote: Wu y Russell concluyeron que Turfanosuchus no era un suquio y ni siquiera un miembro de los Crurotarsi

facts.statement: They also ruled out the possibility of a close relationship with Euparkeria.
facts.quote: Ellos excluyeron también la posibilidad de una relación cercana con Euparkeria

facts.statement: This reassignment was based on the structure of the calcaneum, which is similar to that of other early pseudosuchians, especially aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Esta reasignación estaba basada en la estructura del calcáneo, que es similar a la de otros crurotarsos primitivos, especialmente los aetosaurios

facts.statement: The parent group of Turfanosuchus is Gracilisuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gracilisuchidae

facts.statement: Turfanosuchus belongs to the family Gracilisuchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Gracilisuchidae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Turfanosuchus is Turfanosuchus dabanensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Turfanosuchus dabanensis

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence for the genus Turfanosuchus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
